AI quality / Evidence and accuracy

AI task acceptance accuracy

The percentage of eligible evaluated AI tasks passing every required acceptance check in the client-defined task rubric. A task passes only when all mandatory checks succeed.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of eligible evaluated AI tasks passing every required acceptance check in the client-defined task rubric. A task passes only when all mandatory checks succeed.

%

How we use it

We evaluate whether the system completes the intended work correctly, then inspect failed checks by task type and business impact.

Transparent calculationEligible evaluated tasks passing all acceptance checks / all eligible evaluated tasks in the same sample * 100
tasks passing all checks184
eligible evaluated tasks200

184 / 200 * 100 = 92% task acceptance accuracy for the evaluated sample.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Task type and difficulty
  • Failure criterion and severity
  • Model, prompt, and tool version

Questions we investigate

  • Which acceptance checks fail most often?
  • Does the sample cover difficult production cases?
  • Are automated graders calibrated against reviewers?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Expand representative regression examples.
  • Correct the highest-impact failure modes.
  • Review severity and subgroup results together.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

AI product and evaluation leads
Before releases and after meaningful system changes.

Required data

  • Eligible task inputs and reference outcomes
  • Versioned acceptance rubric and pass labels
  • System versions and sample composition

Read the measure with context

Zero evaluated tasks makes the rate undefined. Acceptance criteria are task-specific rather than a general model score. Uneven sample coverage, class imbalance, grader errors, and severe rare failures can make a single aggregate misleading.
